title: Affine etale splitting of a scheme groupoid at a finite stabilizer
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes [def-weil-size-convention], and let $(V,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$ [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Suppose $V$ is affine, $s,t:R\to V$ are separated, flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, pqf-def-quasifinite]. Separated means closed-immersion diagonal [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $v\in V$ and suppose the stabilizer fibre $G_v$ is finite over $\kappa(v)$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-residue-field]. Here $G=R\times_{V\times_S V,\Delta_V}V$, so its test points are the arrows with equal source and target. There are an affine $S$-scheme $V'$, an etale map $h:V'\to V$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], and a point $v'\in V'$ over $v$ inducing an isomorphism $\kappa(v)\simeq\kappa(v')$, with the following property. Put $R'=R\times_{V\times_S V}(V'\times_S V')$, with the induced groupoid operations and projections $s',t'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There is an open subscheme $P\subseteq R'$ containing the image of the unit and stable under inverse and composition, giving a groupoid $(V',P)$ with the same objects. The restrictions $s'|_P,t'|_P:P\to V'$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Let $G'=R'\times_{V'\times_SV',\Delta_{V'}}V'$ be the stabilizer of $R'$. Every point of the stabilizer fibre $G'_{v'}$ belongs to the open $P$; equivalently $G'_{v'}\times_{R'}P=G'_{v'}$ as schemes. An open subscheme has the restricted structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion]; affine means isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring.

source.place: Tag 0DTE (lemma-splitting-affine-scheme), in Situation 0DTB (situation-splitting), with Definition 04RK (definition-split-at-point), part (2). Finite flat lfp is finite locally free by morphisms.tex Tag 02KB (lemma-finite-flat). We assume local quasi-finiteness everywhere, which implies its required quasi-finiteness along the stabilizer fibre.

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(v)$ and $F=R\times_{s,V}\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change] its structure map is locally quasi-finite, hence locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated] to this map shows every singleton of $F$ is open. Thus $F$ is discrete, has no strict specialization chains, and has dimension at most zero. Apply [lem-sfb-zero-dimensional-field-space-components] to the scheme $F$: its one-point clopen components are spectra of finite-dimensional local Artinian $k$-algebras. The image $E$ of $|G_v|\to|F|$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], applied to the finite map $G_v\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $Z_v$ be the union of the components indexed by $E$. It is clopen and finite over $k$, using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct] finitely many times. The inclusion $G_v\to F$ factors through $Z_v$ because its points lie there, and $e(v)$ lies there. This factorization is surjective on points by the definition of $E$.

source.place: Tag 0DTC (lemma-splitting), second paragraph, the decomposition F_v=Z_v disjoint union Rest; justification by morphisms.tex Tag 01TH and varieties.tex Tag 06LH.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-groupoid-universal-finite-part] to $(V,R)$. Its hypotheses are precisely the separatedness, flatness and local finite presentation assumed here. Obtain the separated etale scheme $g:M\to V$, its universal finite locally free groupoid $(M,Q)$, and the open groupoid immersion $j:Q\hookrightarrow R_M$. The pair $(v:\operatorname{Spec}k\to V,Z_v)$ defines $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to M$. Denote its image by $w$. Then $g(w)=v$. The induced field maps $k\to\kappa(w)\to k$ compose to the identity, so the first map is an isomorphism: the second is an injective field homomorphism fixing $k$, and its image already contains all of $k$. Thus $(M,w)$ is a pointed etale neighbourhood with unchanged residue field. The open $j(Q)$ contains the unit and is stable under inverse and composition, since $j$ is a morphism of groupoids identical on objects.

source.place: Tags 0DTC (lemma-splitting), first two paragraphs, and 0DTD (lemma-splitting-scheme), scheme representability and the point (v,Z_v).

proof.text: We check containment of the whole stabilizer fibre at $w$, not merely of the unit. Represent a point of that fibre by a field-valued loop $z'$ at $a_K$, for an extension $K/k$; let $z\in G_v(K)$ be its image. The map $G_v\to Z_v$ of step 1 is surjective, so [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] says $|(G_v)_K|=|(Z_v)_K|$ inside $|F_K|$. Right translation $r\mapsto c(r,i(z))$ is an automorphism of $F_K$, with inverse $r\mapsto c(r,z)$ by the groupoid laws [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. It maps the subgroup scheme $(G_v)_K$ onto itself. Consequently it preserves the support of the open subscheme $(Z_v)_K$, and therefore preserves that open subscheme with its restricted structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion]. The triple $(a_K,(Z_v)_K,z)$ is a $K$-point of $Q$: $(z,1_K)$ factors through $(G_v)_K$, hence through $(Z_v)_K$ by the factorization of step 1 base changed to $K$. The target formula in [lem-sfb-scheme-groupoid-universal-finite-part] now gives $t_Q(a_K,(Z_v)_K,z)=a_K$. This triple has source $a_K$ too. Its image under $j$ has exactly the same arrow $z$ and endpoints as $z'$, hence equals $z'$ by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Every stabilizer point is therefore in $j(Q)$.

source.place: Tag 0DTC (lemma-splitting), final paragraph, with the translation-invariance verification for the triple made explicit.

proof.text: Since $g:M\to V$ is etale it is unramified [def-weil-etale-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points] makes it locally quasi-finite. The finite locally free source $s_Q:Q\to M$ is finite by [def-pc-finite-locally-free], so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] makes the orbit $O=t_Q(s_Q^{-1}(w))$ finite. Apply [lem-sfb-separated-lqf-affine-finite-set] to the separated locally quasi-finite map $g$, its affine target $V$, and $O$. It gives an affine open containing $O$. Applying [lem-sfb-locally-free-groupoid-invariant-affine] to $(M,Q)$ and $w$ then gives an affine open $B\subseteq M$ containing $O$ and satisfying $s_Q^{-1}(B)=t_Q^{-1}(B)$. In particular $w\in B$, since the unit arrow places $w$ in its orbit.

source.place: Tag 0DTE (lemma-splitting-affine-scheme) through the proof of Tag 04RZ (lemma-strong-splitting-affine-scheme), invariant affine shrinking; more-morphisms.tex Tag 07S0 and groupoids.tex Tag 03JE.

proof.text: Set $V'=B$, $v'=w$, and $h=g|_B$. The map $h$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], since an open immersion is etale. Set $Q_B=s_Q^{-1}(B)=t_Q^{-1}(B)$. By [lem-a1-groupoid-invariant-open-restriction-degree] the groupoid operations restrict to $(B,Q_B)$. Its two projections are the base changes of $s_Q,t_Q$ along $B\hookrightarrow M$: the equality of the inverse images ensures that restriction of both endpoints removes no additional arrows. They remain finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Thus they are finite locally free by the exact definition [def-pc-finite-locally-free], without any Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0DTE through Tag 04RZ, final paragraph: invariant restriction is a base change on each finite projection; morphisms.tex Tags 02KB, 01WG, 01UB, 01TS.

proof.text: The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies $R'=R|_B$ with $B\times_M R_M\times_M B$ by retaining the arrow in $R$ and its two endpoints in $B$. Pull back $j:Q\hookrightarrow R_M$ along $R'\to R_M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] its image $P\subseteq R'$ is open. Its domain is $Q_B$, because $B$ is $Q$-invariant; hence $P$ has the finite locally free projections of step 5. The restricted groupoid morphism is identical on objects, so $P$ contains the full unit and is stable under inverse and composition. A loop at $v'$ in $R'$ is exactly a loop at $w$ in $R_M$ with both endpoints in $B$. Step 3 places every such point in $Q$, and therefore in $Q_B$. Thus the open inverse image of $P$ in $G'_{v'}$ is the whole underlying space. An open subscheme with that underlying space has the entire restricted structure sheaf [def-weil-open-immersion], so $G'_{v'}\times_{R'}P=G'_{v'}$ as schemes. Open restriction changes neither the point nor its residue field; all requested properties now hold.
